$comment: Capability -> provider bindings. The testing skills reason ONLY in terms of the abstract verbs on the left. Nothing in skills/ may name an MCP tool directly, because MCP tool names are the least stable thing in this whole stack. Providers are tried in the listed order.

manual_only_systems.$comment: A capability can resolve 'available: true' -- credentials or a connector are present -- with no executable module in engine/adapters/ behind it. That gap is the worst of both: an agent sees the verb resolve and may assume it can be invoked like github.*, then either hand-roll the call or, worse, infer the content from something else (a commit message, its own reading of the code) and report it as if it came from the system. Every system listed here gets that warning attached to every verb resolution. scripts/validate-repo.mjs cross-checks this list against engine/adapters/index.mjs so it cannot go stale in either direction: dropped here without the adapter shipping, or left here after it does.
manual_only_systems.jira: No executable module yet; see integrations/jira/adapter.md and PROGRESS.md.
manual_only_systems.docs: No Google MCP server was available when this was built; see integrations/google/docs.md. Falls back to state/reports/.
manual_only_systems.drive: No Google MCP server was available when this was built; see integrations/google/drive.md.

gh-cli.notes: Authenticated GitHub CLI. Scope-limited: check `gh auth status` output for the token scopes before assuming write access.

mcp-github.notes: Official GitHub MCP server. Usually requires an OAuth flow that cannot run in a non-interactive session.

jira-rest.notes: Direct Jira Cloud REST v3 fallback when the connector is unavailable.

mcp-playwright.notes: @playwright/mcp. Tool names verified against microsoft/playwright-mcp: browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_take_screenshot, browser_console_messages, browser_network_requests.

builtin-browser.notes: The Claude Code in-app browser pane. Adequate for exploration and evidence capture; it is NOT a test runner.

local-doc-mirror.notes: Always-available fallback: maintain the testing log as versioned Markdown under state/reports/. Honest degradation beats a fake Google Doc.

shell.run.description: Execute a command and capture stdout/stderr/exit code.

github.assign_issue.description: Assignment is NEVER inferred. The user must name the account or state the rule.

browser.explore.description: Open-ended, agent-driven interaction with a running UI. Not reproducible.

browser.run_deterministic_test.description: Run a committed spec file and get a machine-readable result.

http.request.description: Read-only API calls. A request with side effects is an external write and needs authorisation.
